mainEntity.name: Is combining tooth contouring and gum contouring done in one appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some cases, both procedures can be carried out during the same appointment, depending on the extent of treatment required and the clinical approach used. However, your dentist will determine the most appropriate sequence and timing based on your individual circumstances. For more complex cases, a staged approach across separate appointments may be recommended to allow for healing between treatments.

mainEntity.name: Is tooth and gum contouring painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tooth contouring is generally well tolerated and often requires no anaesthetic, as it involves only the enamel layer where there are no nerve endings. Gum contouring is typically performed under local anaesthetic, so discomfort during the procedure itself is minimal. Some tenderness and mild sensitivity in the treated area is common in the days following gum contouring, and your dentist will provide aftercare guidance to help manage this.

mainEntity.name: How long do the results of tooth and gum contouring last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The results of both procedures are considered long-lasting because they involve permanent changes to tooth structure or gum tissue. However, factors such as natural ageing, oral hygiene habits, and lifestyle choices (for example, tooth grinding) can affect how the treated areas look over time. Good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups are important for maintaining results. Your dentist will advise you on what to expect based on your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Are tooth contouring and gum contouring suitable for everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not everyone is a suitable candidate for these procedures. Suitability depends on factors including the thickness of your enamel, the health of your gums, the extent of the changes you are hoping to achieve, and your overall oral health. Patients with active gum disease, significant enamel wear, or more complex aesthetic concerns may be better suited to alternative treatments. A thorough clinical assessment is necessary to determine what is appropriate for each individual.

mainEntity.name: Can gum contouring help with a gummy smile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gum contouring is one treatment option that may be considered for patients with a gummy smile — where a significant portion of the gums is visible when smiling. However, the underlying cause of a gummy smile varies between patients; it may be related to excess gum tissue, the position of the teeth, or in some cases skeletal factors. A clinical assessment is important to identify the cause and determine whether gum contouring, or another approach, is most appropriate.

mainEntity.name: How much enamel can be removed during tooth contouring?

acceptedAnswer.text: The amount of enamel that can safely be removed during tooth contouring is small — typically less than one millimetre. The exact amount depends on the thickness of the enamel in the area being treated and the clinical judgement of your dentist. Removing too much enamel can expose the underlying dentine layer, potentially causing sensitivity. Your dentist will assess enamel thickness and explain the realistic scope of changes before treatment begins.
